verdict.rationale: The evidence shows in-memory building blocks: accessing agent memory, `agent.replay()`, step callbacks that modify memory, and running an agent one step at a time with `agent.step(memory_step)`, framed as useful for long-running tool calls. None of this documents persisting or serializing agent state to durable storage, or resuming a run after a process crash or restart. A developer would have to build checkpointing themselves, which earns no credit as a developer building block, so the verdict is none.

support.subject: As a developer, I can checkpoint agent state so a run can resume exactly where it left off after a crash or restart
